questions.question: A function -

options.A: may or may not need input data
options.B: may or may not return a value

questions.explanation: A C function may take no arguments or several, and may return a value or be void, so neither input nor output is compulsory. Both statements hold, making C correct.

questions.question: If the function returns no value then it is called -
questions.explanation: A function declared with void return type sends nothing back to the caller; you either omit return or write a bare return;. Example: void display(void).

questions.question: What is the limit for number of functions in a C Program?
questions.explanation: The C standard sets no limit on the number of functions a program may define, only practical limits of memory and linker capacity. Hence 'no limit'.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a storage class?
questions.explanation: The four storage classes are auto, register, static and extern. dynamic is not a C storage class at all, so it is the odd one out.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a storage class specifier in C?
questions.explanation: typedef defines a new type name; it is not a storage class. The storage class specifiers are auto, register, static and extern, while volatile is a type qualifier.

questions.question: The machine registers are sometimes called -
questions.explanation: CPU registers that hold arithmetic operands are traditionally called accumulators. The register storage class asks the compiler to keep a variable in such a register for speed.

questions.question: The default storage class of a local variable is -
questions.explanation: A local variable with no storage class specifier is auto by default: it is created on block entry, destroyed on exit and never initialised automatically.

What is the purpose of a function prototype in C?

options.B: To inform the compiler about function signature before definition
options.C: To allocate memory for the function

questions.explanation: A prototype gives the compiler the return type, name and parameter types before the definition, so calls can be type-checked and can appear earlier. It allocates no memory.

questions.question: Which data structure is used by the compiler to manage function calls during recursion?
questions.explanation: Each call pushes an activation record (parameters, locals, return address) onto the run-time stack, and recursion simply pushes more. A queue would give the wrong order.

questions.question: What is the scope and lifetime of a static local variable?

options.A: Scope: Function; Lifetime: Entire program execution
options.C: Scope: Global; Lifetime: Entire program execution

questions.explanation: static gives a local variable function scope but static storage duration: it is invisible outside the function yet keeps its value between calls for the whole program run.

questions.question: In call by value parameter passing, what is passed to the function?
questions.explanation: Call by value copies the argument into the parameter, so the function works on its own copy and the caller's variable is unchanged. Pointers are needed to modify the original.

questions.question: How many values can a function return using the return statement in C?
questions.explanation: The return statement carries exactly one value back, converted to the declared return type. Several results require pointers, a structure or a global variable.

questions.question: What is essential for a recursive function to avoid infinite recursion?
questions.explanation: Every recursion must move toward a base case that stops further calls; without it the stack fills and the program crashes. A loop or a global does not provide that stopping test.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the extern storage class?

options.A: To store variables in CPU registers
options.B: To declare a global variable defined in another file
options.C: To make variables persist between function calls
options.D: To limit variable scope to a function

questions.explanation: extern declares an object or function that is defined in another translation unit and asks the linker to resolve it. It creates no new storage of its own.

questions.question: What is the advantage of using register storage class?

options.B: Faster access as variables are stored in CPU registers

questions.explanation: register asks the compiler to keep the variable in a CPU register to avoid memory access, but it is only a hint that may be ignored, and you cannot take its address.

questions.question: Does C support function overloading (multiple functions with the same name)?

options.A: Yes, based on different parameter types
options.B: Yes, based on different return types
options.C: No, C does not support function overloading
options.D: Yes, but only in C99 standard

questions.explanation: C has no name mangling, so two functions cannot share a name even with different parameters. Overloading is a C++ feature, not standard C.

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of recursion compared to iteration?

options.B: More memory consumption due to stack usage

questions.explanation: Each recursive call keeps its own frame on the stack, so recursion needs more memory than an equivalent loop and can overflow on deep input. Iteration reuses one frame.

questions.question: What is the default initial value of an auto (local) variable in C?
questions.explanation: Automatic variables are not initialised; they hold whatever bytes were left in that stack slot, so the value is garbage. Only static and global objects start at zero.

questions.question: Which header file contains the prototype for the printf() function?
questions.explanation: printf() and scanf() are declared in stdio.h, which must be included to use them. stdlib.h, conio.h and string.h declare other families of functions.
